AWaRe is a classification published by the World Health Organisation (WHO) to categorise antibiotics into Access, Watch, Reserve and Other groups. The grouping take into account the impact of different antibiotics and antibiotic classes on antimicrobial resistance, to emphasize the importance of their appropriate use. The “UK Access, Watch, Reserve, and Other classification for antibiotics” is a UK adapted version of this.
We want to use this classification for OpenPrescrbing Hospitals, but there is no openly available, machine-readable data source mapping products in the dm+d to the classification.
The UKHSA translation table is a static file. Each row is one product. The columns are the structure we want for our own product table. Here, we attempt to create a set of rules that can be used to maintain an up-to-date mapping file as the dm+d data changes.

Step 2: Our dm+d list
This step builds our VMP list. It starts from the UKHSA website list, matches those names to dm+d, and keeps one row for each VMP.

The UKHSA website list
The UKHSA website list is on the UKHSA website. We can’t download it directly, so we have to scrape it. This is a list of antibiotic names and categories. It is not the UKHSA translation table from step 1.

url = "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/uk-aware-antibiotic-classification/uk-access-watch-reserve-and-other-classification-for-antibiotics-uk-aware-antibiotic-classification"

try:
    response = requests.get(url)
    response.raise_for_status()
    soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, "html.parser")
    table = soup.find("table")
    
    data = {
        "Antibiotic": [],
        "England-adapted 2019 AWaRe category": [],
        "UK-adapted 2024 AWaRe category": [],
    }
    
    for table_row in table.tbody.find_all("tr"):
        
        for i,cell in enumerate(table_row.find_all("td")):

We can use more fuzzy matching to get greater sensitivity in the matches.
We include a column ‘match_type’ to let us know if the match is a direct match ‘DIRECT’ or a fuzzy match ‘ASSUMED’.

# Keep a VTM when its name contains the antibiotic name.

    df.join(vtms, how="cross")
    .filter(pl.col("nm").str.contains(pl.col("Antibiotic"), literal=True))
    .with_columns(
        pl.when(pl.col("nm") == pl.col("Antibiotic"))
        .then(pl.lit("DIRECT"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("ASSUMED"))
        .alias("match_type")

The BSA provisional SCMD reports unit dose information for more products than OpenPrescribing Hospitals. This is because the BSA reports unit dose information for products with a Continuous or Not applicable dose form indicator, for which unit doses are not applicable (dose form indicators).
Where both datasets report the unit dose, a small number of products (228) are not reported consistently. This is because the BSA data deviates from the unit dose information in the dm+d (products with different UDFS values). For example, Aciclovir 200mg/5ml oral suspension sugar free has a UDFS of 5 ml and a unit dose unit of spoonful in the dm+d. OpenPrescribing Hospitals holds the same values. The BSA provisional SCMD reports an implied UDFS of 1 ml.

title: Comparing the unit dose reported in the SCMD to the unit dose calculated using the dm+d
text:
Background
The following notice was added to the BSA provisional SCMD on the NHS Business Services Authority (NHSBSA) Open Data Portal on 25/08/2026:

Changes have now been introduced to the Secondary Care Medicines Dataset (SCMD) with the
June 2026 Provisional data release.
The changes include updates to existing column names and the addition of new columns relating to Virtual Medicinal Product (VMP) unit of measure and quantity.
Column name changes
UNIT_OF_MEASURE_NAME → VMP_UDFS_UNIT_OF_MEASURE_NAME
UNIT_OF_MEASURE_IDENTIFIER → VMP_UDFS_UNIT_OF_MEASURE_IDENTIFIER
TOTAL_QUANITY_IN_VMP_UNIT → TOTAL_QUANTITY_IN_VMP_UDFS_UNIT_OF_MEASURE New columns
VMP_UNIT_DOSE_UNIT_OF_MEASURE_NAME – Virtual Medicinal Product (VMP) Unit Dose Unit of Measure name
TOTAL_QUANTITY_IN_VMP_UNIT_DOSE_UNIT_OF_MEASURE – Total quantity in Virtual Medicinal >Product (VMP) Unit Dose Unit of Measure SNOMED code and unit of measure identifier fields are also now provided as string data types.
The Finalised SCMD dataset is published annually and will next be updated in July 2027,
covering data for April 2026 to March 2027. The changes introduced to the Provisional dataset will therefore be reflected in the Finalised dataset as part of this annual update.

The unit dose quantity is a quantity that we have previously had to calculate by linking the SCMD to the dm+d, identifying the UDFS value and unit of measure in the dm+d, and converting the quantity reported in the SCMD to the unit dose quantity. We have described how we do this in our blog post, Calculating unit dose quantity in the Secondary Care Medicines Data.
Inclusion of the unit dose quantity in the raw SCMD will allow us to simplify the processing required for use of the data by OpenPrescribing Hospitals. But before we replace the current unit dose quantity calculation, we need to check that the unit doses now reported in the SCMD agrees with the unit doses we have determined using the extra information available through the dm+d.
Below, we describe this comparison.

title: Comparing the unit dose reported in the SCMD to the unit dose calculated using the dm+d
text:
Methods
The analysis uses two data sources:

The June 2026 BSA provisional SCMD (the only data extract with the additional columns at the time of analysis).
The product information used by OpenPrescribing Hospitals, taken from the dm+d.

To make the comparison, we first identify all of the unique Virtual Medicinal Products (VMPs) that are reported in the June 2026 BSA provisional SCMD. For these products, we identify the UDFS unit of measure from the renamed VMP_UDFS_UNIT_OF_MEASURE_NAME column and the unit dose unit of measure from the VMP_UNIT_DOSE_UNIT_OF_MEASURE_NAME column.
For all of the identified VMPs, we then find the UDFS unit of measure, the UDFS value, and the unit dose unit of measure that are currently used in OpenPrescribing Hospitals.
We compare the UDFS unit of measure and the unit dose unit of measure in the BSA provisional SCMD with the equivalent fields in the OpenPrescribing Hospitals data.
We count the number of VMPs for which these values agree and for which they do not. Where they do not, we split this count out into:

values different - both sources have a UDFS unit of measure, and the values are different
UDFS unit missing in OpenPrescribing Hospitals - the VMP has a UDFS unit of measure in the BSA provisional SCMD, but not in OpenPrescribing Hospitals
UDFS unit missing in the BSA provisional SCMD - the VMP has a UDFS unit of measure in the OpenPrescribing Hospitals data, but not in the BSA provisional SCMD

Where the UDFS units of measure are different, we also report whether the UDFS values are different.
We also identify any VMPs which are reported in the BSA provisional SCMD, but not in the OpenPrescribing Hospitals data.
We then compare unit dose form size (UDFS). The BSA provisional SCMD does not include a UDFS value column, so we have to back-calculate it from the two reported quantity fields. For each organisation row we calculate:
Quantity in the UDFS unit of measure / quantity in the unit dose unit of measure
(We’ve described the differences between unit dose and unit dose form in our blog post, Getting more from the Secondary Care Medicines Data using the Dictionary of Medicines and Devices.)
We first check that this value is the same for all organisation rows of a VMP. A relative difference of 0.1% or less between the minimum and maximum counts as the same.
We then compare that UDFS with UDFS in the OpenPrescribing Hospitals data. We restrict this comparison to VMPs where the UDFS unit of measure already agrees.
We also compare the unit dose unit of measure in the new VMP_UNIT_DOSE_UNIT_OF_MEASURE_NAME column with unit_dose_uom in OpenPrescribing Hospitals. We use the same agreement categories as for the UDFS unit of measure.

title: Comparing the unit dose reported in the SCMD to the unit dose calculated using the dm+d
text:
Conclusions


For all 5,891 VMPs where both sources have a UDFS unit of measure, the units agree for 5,891. OpenPrescribing Hospitals has no UDFS unit for 2,453 VMPs. All of these products have a Continuous or Not applicable dose form indicator, for which unit doses are not applicable. For all of these products, the BSA provisional SCMD UDFS unit is the same as the BSA provisional SCMD unit dose unit and the implied UDFS is 1 on every organisation row. This is consistent with treating the UDFS units as unit dose units for these products.


For the 5,891 VMPs with matching UDFS units, the implied UDFS value agrees for 5,663. 228 have different UDFS values. The most common pair is an implied UDFS of 1 ML in the BSA provisional SCMD and a UDFS of 5 ML in OpenPrescribing Hospitals (221 VMPs). These differences need further investigation.
